From Middle English chele, chile, from Old English ċiele, ċele (“cold; coldness”), from Proto-West Germanic *kali, from Proto-Germanic *kaliz, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to be cold”). Closely related with Dutch kil. Also akin to cool, cold, gel, and congeal, which see.

From Middle English chillen, from Old English ċilian (“to be cold”), from Proto-West Germanic *kilēn (“to be cold”). Cognate with Middle Dutch killen (“to be cold”), Dutch killen (“to be cold, shiver”).

senses.d: A moderate, but uncomfortable and penetrating coldness.
ex: There was a chill in the air.

senses.d: A sudden penetrating sense of cold, especially one that causes a brief trembling nerve response through the body; the trembling response itself; often associated with illness: fevers and chills, or susceptibility to illness.
ex: Close the window or you'll catch a chill.
I felt a chill when the wind picked up.

senses.d: An uncomfortable and numbing sense of fear, dread, anxiety, or alarm, often one that is sudden and usually accompanied by a trembling nerve response resembling the body's response to biting cold.
ex: Despite the heat, he felt a chill as he entered the crime scene.
The actor's eerie portrayal sent chills through the audience.

senses.d: An iron mould or portion of a mould, serving to cool rapidly, and so to harden, the surface of molten iron brought in contact with it.
The hardened part of a casting, such as the tread of a carriage wheel.
A lack of warmth and cordiality; unfriendliness.
ex: His eyes are cold, and the chill between us twists in the pit of my stomach.

senses.d: Calmness; equanimity.
ex: From the very start of the interview, Lawrence's manic energy proved that she had absolutely no chill.
Granted, Tyrese put himself out there by even posting the video, knowing the internet has no chill.

senses.d: A sense of style; trendiness; savoir faire.
ex: Will and Grace still have no chill; having a pillow fight in the Oval Office proves that.
Angelina left Brad, which upsets me because I'm human," said Corden, adding that Netflix had chill, but the FBI had "zero chill."

senses.d: A chilling effect; an atmosphere of this.
Moderately cold or chilly.
ex: A chill wind was blowing down the street.
Noisome winds, and blasting vapours chill.

senses.d: Unwelcoming; not cordial.
ex: Arriving late at the wedding, we were met with a chill reception.

senses.d: Calm, relaxed, easygoing.

Paint-your-own ceramics studios are a chill way to express yourself while learning more about your date's right brain.

senses.d: "Cool"; meeting a certain hip standard or garnering the approval of a certain peer group.

senses.d: Okay, not a problem.
ex: Sorry about that. —It's chill.

senses.d: To lower the temperature of something; to cool.
ex: Chill before serving.

senses.d: To become cold.
ex: In the wind he chilled quickly.

senses.d: To harden a metal surface by sudden cooling.
To become hard by rapid cooling.
To relax; to lie back; to take things easy.
ex: Chill, man, we've got a whole week to do it; no sense in getting worked up.
The new gym teacher really has to chill or he's gonna blow a gasket.

senses.d: To "hang", hang out; to spend time with another person or group.

senses.d: To smoke marijuana.

senses.d: To discourage, depress.
ex: Censorship chills public discourse.

From clippings of attributive use of China, q.v., the country in East Asia. In reference to porcelain and porcelain objects, via clipping of chinaware and via this sense of Persian چینی (čīnī /čini) in Persia and India, which influenced the pronunciation (see below). In reference to medicine, via clipping of China root. In reference to flowers, via clipping of China rose. In reference to tea, via clipping of China tea. In Cockney slang, a clipping of china plate as a rhyme of mate (“friend”).

senses.d: Synonym of porcelain, a hard white translucent ceramic made from kaolin, now (chiefly US) sometimes distinguished in reference to tableware as fine or good china.
ex: It's a china doll.

senses.d: Chinaware: porcelain tableware.
ex: ...a Present of certain very rich Pieces of China.
He set the table with china, cloth napkins, and crystal stemware.

senses.d: Cheaper and lower-quality ceramic and ceramic tableware, distinguished from porcelain.
Synonym of China root, the root of Smilax china (particularly) as a medicine.
ex: China, saith Manardus, makes a good colour in the face, takes away melancholy, and all infirmities proceeding from cold […].

senses.d: Synonym of cheyney: worsted or woolen stuff.

senses.d: Synonym of China rose, in its various senses.

senses.d: Synonym of mate (rhyme of china-plate).
